headline: Turning Meetings into Instant Enterprise-Grade Artifacts
subtitle: AI in Teams converts spoken intent into ready-to-use PPT and docs, unlocking monetization and deepening the Microsoft 365 moat.
visual_design: Simple title layout with a one-line punchline and a right-hand column listing team, date, and context ('For Microsoft use only').

headline: Manual doc creation is slowing execution and wasting talent
subtitle: High-value meetings still require hours of post-processing to become actionable PPT/Word outputs.
speaker_intent: Align leaders that current meeting-to-document workflows destroy productivity and dilute meeting ROI.

sections.title: Meetings drive outcomes, but artifacts drive execution

bullets.text: Modern knowledge work outcomes are encoded in PPT decks, Word specs, and ADO items—not in raw meeting transcripts.
Teams is already the hub where critical discussions happen across audio, video, chat, and shared files.

citation.location: Product: Doc Co-creation Agent in Teams

bullets.text: 30M PowerPoint files are created per day, underscoring how central slide artifacts are to enterprise communication.

sections.title: Current workflows separate discussion from document creation

bullets.text: In-meeting discussions and doc creation are two separate workflows, forcing users to switch tools and contexts after every important meeting.
Participants must manually translate meeting content into specs, slide decks, and ADO items, often hours or days after the conversation.

visual_design: Two-column framework: left column 'Today: Meetings' and right column 'Today: Artifacts', connected by a large gap arrow labeled 'Manual translation gap'.

headline: The productivity gap is now a competitive and monetization risk
subtitle: Human bottlenecks, design skill gaps, and new AI players create a crisis of inaction.
speaker_intent: Create urgency that failing to close this gap cedes value to competitors and limits Copilot revenue.

bullets.text: Employees spend disproportionate hours on formatting and layout instead of high-value strategic thinking.
The 'blank page' problem makes it hard to synthesize raw notes into concise, structured slide narratives, delaying decisions.
Most professionals lack design skills to produce polished, enterprise-ready decks, leading to rework and frustration.

sections.title: Competitors are attacking the doc creation pain point

bullets.text: Gamma has over 70M users focused on AI-first slide and document creation, validating strong user demand for 'no-PPT-skill' workflows.

citation.location: Gamma app has more than 70M users

bullets.text: Gemini and other AI competitors already summarize meetings and generate content, increasing pressure on Microsoft to differentiate.

sections.title: Missed opportunity to monetize Copilot and deepen the moat

bullets.text: Without a 'killer app' like one-click PPT from meetings, Copilot risks being perceived as a 'nice to have' instead of essential to workflow.
If third-party apps become the default for AI-generated slides, Microsoft loses data gravity and weakens the Office and Teams ecosystem.

visual_design: Issue tree chart (consulting-style) breaking the central problem 'Productivity gap & competitive risk' into three branches: Human Bottleneck, Competitors, Monetization Risk.

headline: AI in Teams can turn spoken intent into instant artifacts
subtitle: A doc co-creation agent generates PPT/Word directly from meeting and chat context.
speaker_intent: Introduce the solution clearly and early as the natural answer to the gap.

bullets.text: Develop a doc co-creation agent in Teams that generates PPT and Word based on meeting audio/video, chats, and channel context.

citation.location: What: Develop a doc co-creation agent in Teams

bullets.text: Enable Teams users to collaboratively create, review, and edit documents in real time, within the same app where discussions happen.

citation.location: enabling Teams users to collaboratively create

bullets.text: Extend the content generation engine to other Microsoft surfaces such as SharePoint for broader leverage.

citation.location: extended to other content platforms such as SharePoint

sections.title: From 'talk' to 'artifact' in a single workflow

bullets.text: AI understands the evolving conversation and generates structured artifacts—updated ADO items, presentation-ready slides, detailed specs—in real time.

citation.location: By enabling AI to do both...

bullets.text: Meetings become active, real-time generators of actionable, high-quality outputs instead of passive discussions that require follow-up work.

citation.location: This is the future of meeting productivity

visual_design: Before/After flow diagram: 'Spoken Intent' → (Today: Transcript → Manual Work → PPT/Word) vs. (Future: AI Agent in Teams → Instant PPT/Word/ADO).

headline: PPT Maker in Teams unifies discussion and document creation
subtitle: A Teams-native interface for co-creating polished, narrative-driven decks during the meeting.
speaker_intent: Make the solution tangible and show how users will experience it.

bullets.text: A 'PPT Maker' surface embedded in Teams with a conversation panel for instructions and refinement.
A live preview window where users can review AI-generated slides, such as technical or product narratives.

citation.location: A Preview window where users can review slides

bullets.text: Standard slide controls—navigation, thumbnails, full-screen—ensure familiarity and low adoption friction.

citation.location: Controls for navigation, thumbnails, and full-screen mode

bullets.text: Multiple participants can guide, review, and edit the AI-generated deck in real time, leveraging Teams’ collaboration strengths.
Users can iterate on storyline and design during the meeting, eliminating the 'after the meeting' document scramble.

citation.location: We want to unify them within a single app

visual_design: Wireframe-style layout: left pane 'Conversation & Controls', right pane 'Slide Preview & Thumbnails' to illustrate the in-Teams experience.

headline: Orchestrated AI workflow makes high-quality artifacts feasible
subtitle: A modular pipeline mines enterprise data, weaves narrative, structures content, and assembles polished outputs.
speaker_intent: Demonstrate technical feasibility and thoughtfulness of the architecture to de-risk execution concerns.

bullets.text: An Orchestrator with a Dispatcher plans tasks based on user input, slides, context, and instructions.
A Miner extracts 'Facts' from enterprise data—meetings, chats, docs—into a structured content pool of atoms such as architecture, metrics, and code.
A Weaver generates narration while a Structurer organizes slides and chapters into coherent storylines.

citation.location: Content Creation: A Weaver handles narration

bullets.text: An Assembler manages layout and style, using engines like HTML, FFMPEG, and python-pptx to produce final artifacts (HTML, PPTX, DOCX, MP4).

citation.location: Final Output: An Assembler manages layout

bullets.text: Multi-modal grounding on audio/video, chats, shared files, and meeting histories is a unique advantage of Teams and Microsoft 365.
The same pipeline can output multiple formats, enabling reuse across PowerPoint, Word, SharePoint, and even video summaries.

citation.location: Final Output: ... Artifact (HTML, PPTX, DOCX, MP4)

visual_design: Process flow diagram (left-to-right) with four blocks: Orchestrator → Miner → Weaver/Structurer → Assembler/Engine → Artifacts; use a consulting-style process chart.

headline: Teams has a structural advantage competitors cannot easily copy
subtitle: Owning meetings, file formats, and AI lets us deliver unmatched fidelity and integration.
speaker_intent: Reinforce that Microsoft is uniquely positioned to win this space and defend against Gemini/Gamma.

bullets.text: Microsoft owns the meeting data (Teams), the file standards (PPTX/DOCX), and the AI layer (Copilot), enabling deep integration.
Competitors can summarize meetings but cannot natively generate high-fidelity, editable Microsoft Office documents as seamlessly.
Teams has unique multi-modal context—audio, video, chat, shared files, meeting histories—that can be used to ground AI outputs.
By moving doc creation inside Teams, we transform it from a communication tool into the 'OS of work'.
If the best way to draft a document is to 'have a meeting about it', users are incentivized to host more discussions and store more data in Microsoft 365.
This increases time-in-app, reduces churn, and enriches the Teams ecosystem versus third-party platforms.

visual_design: 2x2 matrix comparing Microsoft vs. competitors on axes: 'Owns Collaboration Surface' and 'Owns Document Standard & AI'; highlight Microsoft in the top-right quadrant.

headline: Doc co-creation is a Copilot monetization and retention engine
subtitle: One-click PPT becomes the tangible, high-frequency use case that justifies Copilot pricing.
speaker_intent: Connect the solution directly to ARPU uplift and strategic business value.

sections.title: From 'nice to have' to 'must have' Copilot

bullets.text: One-click PPT generation from meetings is a clear, high-value feature that directly supports the $30/month Copilot for Microsoft 365 price point.
High-frequency usage in everyday meetings turns Copilot into an essential workflow tool rather than an occasional assistant.
Deep integration between Teams, Office formats, and Copilot creates a defensible loop that is difficult for Zoom, Slack, or standalone apps to replicate.
More meetings and artifacts in Teams increase data gravity, further improving AI quality and reinforcing user lock-in.

visual_design: Flywheel diagram: 'Doc Co-Creation in Teams' → 'Higher Copilot Usage' → 'Stronger Justification for $30 ARPU' → 'More Data in Ecosystem' → back to 'Better Doc Co-Creation'.

headline: Execution needs focused engineering and design investment
subtitle: A small, senior-heavy team can tackle narrative quality, aesthetics, and evaluation challenges.
speaker_intent: Show we understand the hard parts and have a realistic, contained ask to address them.

bullets.text: Achieving a 'WOW' effect in generated slides requires strong aesthetic evaluation and systematic narrative capabilities.
We need robust datasets and evaluation metrics to ensure outputs meet enterprise standards for style and storytelling.
Current limitation: SOX CMD does not have enough resources to take full ownership of this project.
Ask: 6 developers (including at least 3 senior engineers) to build and harden the orchestrated backend and Teams integration.
Ask: Dedicated designer resources to define aesthetic and narrative evaluation metrics and guide template systems.

citation.location: Designer resource, important for defining Eval metrics

bullets.text: We are open to integrating with existing services (e.g., Societas) where capabilities are ready, to accelerate delivery.

citation.location: We are open to integrate with any services

visual_design: Gantt-style or responsibility matrix-style chart outlining streams: 'Backend & Orchestration', 'Teams UX & Integration', 'Aesthetic & Narrative Evaluation', mapped to the requested dev and designer roles.

headline: Decision: Fund Teams doc co-creation as the AI killer app
subtitle: Approve resources to make Teams the place where every meeting ends with a finished artifact.
speaker_intent: Drive to a clear go/no-go decision and reinforce the strategic upside of approval.

sections.title: What we are asking leadership to approve

bullets.text: Greenlight the Teams-native doc co-creation agent as a strategic Copilot and Teams investment.

citation.location: Develop a doc co-creation agent in Teams

bullets.text: Allocate 6 developers (3 senior+) and dedicated designer(s) to build the orchestrated workflow, PPT Maker UX, and evaluation framework.
Teams becomes the default way to turn meetings into enterprise-grade PPT/Word artifacts, in real time.

citation.location: This is the future of meeting productivity

bullets.text: Copilot adoption and perceived value increase, supported by a daily, high-impact use case that competitors cannot easily match.

citation.location: Drive Copilot Monetization / Hard to Copy

bullets.text: Microsoft strengthens its position as the 'OS of work' by unifying communication, collaboration, and document creation in Teams.
